title: Tanzanian Peanut Vegetable Stew
community: Popular across central and western Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mboga ya Karanga — mixed vegetables simmered in a rich peanut sauce with tomatoes and spices. The inland Tanzanian alternative to coconut-based vegetables — peanuts provide the richness and creaminess that coconut milk provides on the coast.
longDesc: Peanut vegetable stew is the inland Tanzanian counterpart to the coastal coconut vegetable preparations — where the coast uses coconut milk for richness, the interior uses groundnuts. The result is a deeply satisfying, protein-enriched vegetable stew.
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes — peeled and cubed
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, curry powder, paprika, and tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes.
Add sweet potato and carrot. Stir to coat.
Add 1.5 cups water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add green beans and cabbage. Simmer 8 more minutes.
Mix peanut butter with ½ cup warm water. Add to pot.
Simmer 5 minutes until sauce is thick and creamy.
chefTips: Mix peanut paste with warm water first — prevents lumping.
Add harder vegetables first, softer ones later.
The peanut sauce thickens significantly — add a little water if too thick.
commonMistakes: Adding all vegetables at once — different cooking times.
cookingScience: The peanut butter contains naturally occurring emulsifiers (lecithin) that allow the fat and water to form a stable sauce without separating — producing a naturally creamy, smooth consistency without dairy.
sustainabilityTips: All vegetables locally grown in Tanzania; peanuts are nitrogen-fixing.
healthBenefits: Complete nutrition — protein from peanuts, vitamins from vegetables.
culturalNote: Peanut vegetable stew is the inland Tanzania equivalent of coconut vegetable curry — each region uses the richest, most available fat source to transform simple vegetables into something deeply satisfying.
